package_info.why_malicious: The subdomain cdn2.cocoapods.org, previously used by CocoaPods as a CDN for package distribution, was abandoned but its DNS records continued to point to GitHub Pages. Attackers hijacked the subdomain by claiming it on GitHub Pages and hosted a casino website, enabling potential phishing, malware distribution, or brand impersonation attacks under the guise of a trusted software supply chain domain.

execution_context.trigger: DNS resolution or user navigation to the subdomain
execution_context.file_location: cdn2.cocoapods.org (served via GitHub Pages repository controlled by attacker)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious casino website content (HTML/JavaScript) hosted at https://cdn2.cocoapods.org/, including scripts and assets unrelated to CocoaPods.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user or automated system navigates to cdn2.cocoapods.org, the DNS resolves to a GitHub Pages site controlled by the attacker, which serves casino website content via HTML and JavaScript, resulting in the exposure of users to phishing, malware, or deceptive branding.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A critical infrastructure subdomain for a major package manager is serving unrelated gambling content, which is a strong indicator of subdomain hijacking and potential for malicious use.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate CocoaPods subdomains should only serve official package files, documentation, or static assets. Serving third-party gambling or unrelated content from this domain is a clear violation of expected behavior for trusted developer infrastructure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve serving CocoaPods package files, documentation, or static assets required for package management. Hosting unrelated or third-party content is never expected.
key_indicators: Abandoned subdomain (cdn2.cocoapods.org) with DNS records still pointing to GitHub Pages
Presence of casino/gambling HTML and JavaScript content on a trusted developer infrastructure domain
Mismatch between expected content (package files, documentation) and actual content (gambling site)
Potential for phishing, malware distribution, or brand impersonation via a trusted subdomain

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies that the subdomain cdn2.cocoapods.org is abandoned but its DNS records still point to GitHub Pages.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker is able to claim the subdomain on GitHub Pages.

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates a GitHub Pages repository and configures it to serve content at cdn2.cocoapods.org.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control over the content served from the trusted subdomain.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads and serves a malicious casino website (HTML/JavaScript) from the hijacked subdomain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users and automated systems accessing cdn2.cocoapods.org are exposed to phishing, malware distribution, or deceptive content under the trusted CocoaPods brand.

behavioral_signatures: Trusted infrastructure subdomains (e.g., cdn2.cocoapods.org) serving content unrelated to their official purpose, such as gambling or phishing sites
Sudden change in content type or appearance on developer infrastructure domains
Abandoned subdomains with DNS records pointing to third-party hosting platforms (e.g., GitHub Pages) but no official repository
file_indicators: CNAME or A records for critical subdomains (e.g., cdn2.cocoapods.org) pointing to GitHub Pages (e.g., username.github.io)
Unexpected HTML/JavaScript files containing gambling or phishing content on infrastructure subdomains
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to cdn2.cocoapods.org (or similar trusted subdomains) returning non-official or suspicious content
Unusual traffic patterns to developer infrastructure domains with content types inconsistent with package distribution (e.g., casino site assets, gambling scripts)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor DNS records for critical infrastructure subdomains to ensure they do not point to third-party hosting unless actively managed. Regularly scan and crawl subdomains for unexpected changes in content type, especially for developer or package manager domains. Set up alerts for sudden appearance of unrelated content (e.g., gambling, phishing) on trusted subdomains. Use automated web crawlers to verify that subdomains only serve expected package files or documentation, and flag any deviation for investigation.
